translations.text: Concerning how Maccabeus encountered the Jews in Mesopotamia of Syria and killed them in their valleys as far as the surroundings of Jerusalem, from Jabbok, and concerning the destruction of the holy city [?].

For they advanced from Samaria as far as the surroundings of Jerusalem and all its districts, and killed with the edge of the sword until they left only a few survivors. For the Edomites, Syrians, and Amalekites joined with Maccabeus the Moabite, who destroyed the city of Jerusalem.
When the children of Israel sinned, he sent them Maccabeus the Moabite, and he killed them all in a slaughter.
Because of this matter, God's enemy [?] against his holy city, and they joined together in their warfare.
The Edomites and the Philistines joined together and began taking vengeance on the city of the Lord, for he himself had sent them because its people had scorned the word of the Lord.
As for Maccabeus, his city was Ramath in Moab. He rose up in strength from his city and joined together with those who were with him.

They planned in the valleys of Gelabuhe [?], from Mesopotamia to Syria, to destroy the city of God. From there he asked the Philistines and Amalekites for help and gave them much gold and silver, horses and chariots, so that they would join him in warfare.
They came together and devastated the city, pouring out the blood of those who lived in it like water.

They made Jerusalem like a grain watchman's hut. They committed filthy and foul acts within it, and everything displeasing to the Lord—impure deeds. They defiled the city of the Lord, which was full of righteousness and holiness.
They made the corpses of your servants food for the birds of the sky, and the flesh of your righteous people food for the wild animals.

They slaughtered adults and children, and they tore out what was in the wombs of pregnant women, until the Lord, who examines hearts and kidneys, became angry. For they acted without fear of the Lord, as Satan had taught them.
They returned to their own territories, rejoicing over the evil they had done to the people of the Lord, and taking the captives and the plunder they had seized from the holy city.
When they entered and returned to their dwellings, they celebrated with rejoicing, merriment, and singing.
The prophet whom they called Reai said to him: “Rejoice a little now in the light of this hour. The Lord, the Holy One of Israel, will take vengeance on you in a way you have not imagined.
You say, ‘My horses are swift runners, and therefore I will escape quickly.’
But I tell you that those who pursue you will run faster than eagles, and you will not escape [?] or the wrath of the Lord that is upon you.

Will you say, ‘I will put on iron armor, and neither an arrow's shot nor the throwing of spears can overcome me’? [?] ‘I will not take vengeance on you in that way, by hurling iron,’ says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel. ‘Instead, I will bring a grievous pain into your heart, worse than an arrow's shot, the throwing of a spear, or the disease of scabies and sores.

I will bring grievous suffering into your heart. You will seek someone to help you but will find no one, for my wrath has struck you. You will not escape from my hand until I erase your memory from the earth.

You will know that I am the Lord your creator when I do this swiftly, in the blink of an eye. For you have stiffened your neck and raised your head against my city. You are like grass before the wind, which fire consumes before my eyes, and like dust that winds and a whirlwind sweep away from the face of the earth. That is what you are before me.
For I have given you my wrath, and you have not acknowledged your Creator. I, too, will show no favor to anything that belongs to you, and I will leave no one in all your mountains to tell of it.’”

Now repent of all the evil you have done. If you repent and humble yourself before the Lord with tears and weeping, and appeal to him with a pure heart, the Lord will pass over your sin and all the offenses you have committed before him.
At that time Maccabeus wept before the Lord because of his sin and covered himself with dust, for the Lord had rebuked him.

He knew that the Lord would not hold back the disaster he had spoken of through his prophet. For his eyes are watchful, and he does not sleep; his ears are open, and he is not deaf. The word he has spoken will not prove false, and he will carry it out all at once, in the blink of an eye.
He cast off his clothes and put on sackcloth made of hair. He put dust on his head and wept and cried out before the Lord his God because of the evil he had done.
The prophet spoke to him, for Ramoth of Moab is near Syria.
He dug into the ground and entered it up to his neck. He wept bitterly and repented of the sin he had committed before the Lord.

The Lord said this to the prophet in the land of Judah: “Go to the land of Ramoth, to Maccabeus, the ruler of Moab, and tell him: ‘The Lord says this: You were not the one who did this, so do not boast [?], “By the strength of my power and by my cunning I destroyed the holy city.” Rather, I am the Lord, your king. I myself sent you, by my will, to destroy my city.
For she rebelled against me through all her greed, her sexual immorality, and her hostility.

I rejected her and handed her over to you. It was not because of you that this happened, yet you stiffened your neck and said, “I devastated the city by the strength of my own hand.” Now, because of the children you have fathered, the Lord has passed over your sin.
Now repent with all your heart and be steadfast. Do not waver, for those who waver are not steadfast in repentance.
Blessed are those who repent with all their hearts and do not return to filth and sin in any of the things for which they repent because of their evil deeds.
They are steadfast in weeping, in tears, in much pleading, and in bowing down before the Lord who created them. For he says to those who repent, “After you went astray and repented, you are mine.”

To the proud man, too, after he had gone astray and returned to him in repentance, he said: “Because of your trembling and your fear, I will pass over your sin. For I am the Lord, your [?], who visits a father's sin upon his children to the third and fourth generation. But to those who love me and keep my commandments, I show mercy to the [?] generation.

Now, because of these children you have fathered, I will keep my covenant with you, and I will accept the repentance that I made on account of your evil deeds,” says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, who rules over all.’”

At that time he came out of the pit and bowed down before the prophet, saying: “May the Lord do such and such to me if I am separated from you! Make me whatever you wish, for I rebelled against the Lord and did not follow his commandment, just as my fathers did not. We have no law, and you yourself know that we worship idols as our fathers taught us.

Until now I have not listened to the words of the Lord's prophets. For I am a sinner who has walked in my sin, in the pride of my heart, and in my stubbornness. I rebelled against the Lord's commandment and did not follow his commandment or the judgments he commanded me to observe.”
The prophet answered him: “I know that he has now accepted your repentance, for no one among your kindred before you has acknowledged his sin.

From now on, abandon the worship of idols and return to the knowledge of the Lord, so that your repentance may be genuine.” He bowed down at the prophet's feet, and the prophet raised him up and instructed him in everything appropriate to good conduct.
He did as the Lord commanded him and returned to his house.
Maccabeus set himself right and removed from his house all sorcery and idols, diviners, idol worshipers, and sorcerers.

And he questioned the captive children whom they had brought from Jerusalem, evening and morning, about all the commandments of the Lord, his law and his ordinances, and how their fathers observed them.
And he appointed some of the wise men among the captives to serve in his house.

And again, from among their wise young men, he appointed attendants in his bedchamber to look after his young children as their companions, so that they might teach them the way of the Lord, as the children of Israel observed his law, his ordinances, his judgments and his justice. And he heard from the captives about all their prohibitions, concerning things from which the Moabites abstained.

And he abolished their prohibitions and all their [?], all their idols, all their [?], and their sacrifices from their fattened animals, from the vines of his pastures and from roasted goats, which he sacrificed to his gods evening and morning.
And he sacrificed to them and worshiped them in every undertaking, at every time and hour. He petitioned them, trusted in them and did their will in everything that the demons, his gods, told him.
And he did not depart from their word in anything they told him, because he thought that they had saved him in everything.
But Maccabeus abandoned their way.

And when Zerai heard the words that the prophet spoke to him, he made his way good through repentance. All his household made their ways better than those of the children of Israel in those days. For the children of Israel would rebel against him at one time, and when he punished them, they would acknowledge him and cry out to the Lord.

And when he saw that they had been humiliated under the hands of those who oppressed them, and that they cried out before him, then he would have mercy on them, remembering the covenant with their fathers when they cried out to him, for the sake of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, their fathers.
And when he had saved them, they would forget the one who had saved them and return to the worship of idols.

Then he would send nations against them to oppress them. And when they oppressed them and caused them pain, they would cry out to the Lord. Then he would have mercy on them and show them compassion, because he loved them, for they were the work of his hands.
And again, when he gave them respite, they would return to provoking him by worshiping the idols around them and by the evil work of their hands.

And he would raise up against them the peoples of Philistia, Moab, Midian, Syria and Egypt. They would weep and cry out when their enemies defeated them, afflicted them, forced them to labor and enslaved them. And he would raise up judges for them, so that the judges might save them.
And this happened in the days of Hoshea.
And this happened in the days of Gideon.

And this happened in the days of Samson, Barak, Deborah, and Judith. Whether from among women or from among men, he raises up judges for them to save them from those who torment them and to rescue them from the hand of all their enemies.
As he wills, the Lord saves them from those who torment them.
You rejoice greatly in everything he has made flourish for them in the crops of their land, and in his multiplying their livestock and all the pasture in the fields and the wilderness.

He blesses their livestock and their plants. He blesses everything they possess, both at home and in the wilderness, and does not let their livestock diminish. For he watches over them with his eyes and loves them greatly, because they are the offspring of the righteous.
But when they themselves become evil in their deeds, he delivers them into the hands of their enemies.
When he kills them, they seek him in the morning, turn back, and go to the Lord their creator.

When they return with all their hearts, he forgives them and does not remember their former offenses against them. For he knows that they are flesh and blood and that they are subject to the deception of the thoughts of this world and of demons.
When Maccabeus heard this word that the Lord had ordained on the mountain of his sanctuary, he struggled earnestly in repentance.

He did not stray in his conduct from what he had seen and heard in this account, or from all the good things the children of Israel did, because God had mercy on them. When God punished them for transgressing the commandment, they wept and cried out, and he again had mercy on them, and they kept his commandment.
Likewise, Maccabeus also made his ways upright, kept his commandment, and walked according to the commandment of the Lord, the God of Israel.
Knowing this from what he had heard, he likewise placed his trust in everything in which the children of Israel trusted, by keeping the Lord’s commandment.
He directed his household and his children to walk in all the ways and commandments of the Lord.

And he himself abstained from the things from which the Jews abstained. He also observed the commandments that the Jews kept, doing according to what he had heard. He abstained from the foods from which the Jews abstained, although he belonged to another people and was a Moabite.
He also gave tithes and gave the firstborn of his sheep, cattle, and donkeys, and of everything he had acquired. He likewise offered the sacrifices that the Jews offered, facing toward Jerusalem.
Those offered for vows, those offered for sin, freewill offerings, offerings for deliverance, and regular offerings.
He likewise offered the firstfruits and the libations that the Jews offered, and gave them to the Levite [?] whom he had appointed. He did everything the Jews did, including burning incense.
And he made [?] and [?], tables, curtains, basins, [?], and [?] for the holy lamps, and veils, as they make within Israel’s Holy of Holies, if they pleased the Lord.
For they lived according to his law and his ordinance, and if God was not angry with them and did not deliver them into the hands of their enemies, Maccabeus likewise made all his ways good.
And at all times he prayed to the Lord, the God of Israel, that he might be his guide and not separate him from the congregation of Israel, whom he had chosen and who did his will.

And again he prayed that he might give him descendants in Zion and houses in Jerusalem, that he might save him from the [?] of which he had spoken through the mouth of the prophet, and that he might accept his repentance for everything of which he had repented.
And he wept with tears before the Lord, asking that he not wipe out his descendants from the earth and that he protect him in his coming in and his going out.

And some of the people of Moab who were under the authority of Maccabeus began to believe, because their messenger walked in a right way. They considered his justice and did his will. They despised the justice of their cities and the [?] of their country, and saw that the way of Maccabeus was more upright and far better.
And they came to him and listened to the justice, righteousness and goodness of Maccabeus.
And he possessed much livestock, male and female slaves, donkeys and camels. He also had horses clothed in iron.
And from the day he began to worship the Lord, whenever he went into battle, no one defeated him; rather, he himself was the victor.
And they would come in the strength of their gods to fight against him, and curse him in the name of their gods. But no one could defeat him, because he had placed his trust in the Lord his God.
And he continued to act in this way, defeating his enemies and bringing nations under his authority.
He took vengeance on behalf of the oppressed and upheld justice for orphans.
He welcomed widows and orphans in their distress, fed the hungry from his provisions, and clothed the naked from his clothing.

And he rejoiced in his deeds and in the work of his hands. He gave from what he possessed without withholding anything, and he gave a tenth to the house of the Lord. While Maccabeus was doing these things, he died peacefully.

He left his offspring as young children, and they grew up as their father had instructed them. They kept the order of their household and guarded everything they owned, and they did not oppress the poor, the orphan, or the stranger.

They feared the Lord and gave their possessions as alms to the poor. They held fast to everything their father had entrusted to them. They comforted widows and orphans in their distress and became a father and mother to them. They rescued them from the hands of their oppressors and comforted them in every trouble and sorrow that befell them.
They continued living in this way.
After him came Tsirutsaydan, king of the Chaldeans. He destroyed their entire city, and they took the children of Maccabeus captive, and he destroyed their whole land.

He plundered all their possessions, and idol worshipers seized them themselves and took them into their country. These people do not walk according to the Lord’s commandment and judgment, but in every kind of evil, sexual immorality, uncleanness, greed, and abuse, without remembering their God.

They do not eat any dead animal, blood, anything eaten by a wild beast, anything torn apart, or anything displeasing to the Lord. There is no law from among all the commandments of righteousness written in the Law.
They do not acknowledge the Lord as their Creator and Savior, who brought them out of their mother’s womb and nourished them with what they needed.

They have no law governing justice. They walk in [?], insolence, sexual immorality, and uncleanness, marrying their father’s wife and their mother’s sister. They commit every kind of evil and marry their sisters and their relatives. They have no law.
All their ways are slippery, dark, unclean, and sexually immoral.

But the children of Maccabeus observe all their prohibitions. They do not eat dead animals or anything torn apart, and they keep themselves from all the uncleanness and sins of the Chaldeans. For the evil deeds committed by the [?]—sinners, rebels, heretics, and shameless people, full of filth, uncleanness, and insolence—are many and are not written in this book.
There is nothing about them that pleases the Lord their Creator.

Furthermore, they worship an idol named Baal-peor. They worship it and trust in it as though it were the Lord their Creator, although it is deaf and mute and can neither see nor hear. It is a carved image, the work of human hands, cast by a metalworker in gold and silver, the work—the work—of a human being, without understanding or breath.
It neither eats nor drinks.
It neither kills nor gives life.
He neither planted nor destroyed.
He neither acted cruelly nor did good.
It does not [?], nor does it make anyone rich.
It neither punishes nor shows mercy, but is only a snare for leading astray the foolish people of the Chaldeans.
The arrogant Tsirutsaydan, the enemy of the Lord, appointed false priests and [?] of the gods.
They offer sacrifices to them and [?] to them.
He thinks that they are the ones who eat and drink.
He gave cattle, sheep, heifers, and goats to the idols [?]. They offered sacrifices evening and morning, and he ate from that unclean sacrifice.
They did not do this only themselves; they also threatened other people and forced them to sacrifice to their gods.

When they saw that the children of Maccabeus were good and worshiped the Lord their Creator, those [?] of the gods wanted to lead them astray so that they would sacrifice and eat from that unclean sacrifice. But these blessed men refused them.
They could not get them to say yes, because they kept their father’s commandment, persevered in doing good, and feared the Lord all the more.
Then they accused them, insulted them, and attacked them.
They told King Tsirutsaydan that they had refused to bow down and sacrifice to his gods.
Because of this, the king became angry and distressed. He ordered them to be brought, and they brought them and stood them before him. He said to them, “Sacrifice and bow down to my gods.”
They answered him, “We will not obey you in this matter, and we will not sacrifice to your unclean gods.”
He tried to frighten them in many ways, but he could not overcome them, because they had made their hearts firm in devotion to the Lord.
He kindled a fire and put them into it, and they surrendered their souls to the Lord.
After their death, they appeared to him alive, holding their sharpened swords, while he was sleeping at night in his royal bed. He was greatly afraid.
He said to them, “What shall I do for you, my lords? Spare me, and do not take my life, so that I may do everything you command me.” They terrified him still more.

They told him everything necessary, saying, “Remember that God is your Creator, and that there is one who will bring you down from this pride of yours and cast you into the depths of hell with the devil, your father. There you will undergo your full punishment, because you burned us with fire, although we had done you no wrong, while we worshiped God our Creator and bowed down to him in fear of God.
For he is the Creator of everything, who made heaven, earth, the sea, and everything in it:
The sun, the moon, the stars, and all creation, which the Lord himself created.
There is no other God besides him in heaven above or on earth below. He can do everything, and nothing is beyond him. He kills and gives life; he punishes and shows mercy.
No one can escape from his hand, for he is the ruler of heaven and earth.

Nothing that he created transgresses his command except you, rebel, and rebels like you, whose hearts your father Satan has blinded. They, you, and your gods will descend together into Gehenna, from which there is no escape forever.
For you are not doing this by yourself. Rather, Satan is your teacher, who taught you this evil conduct so that you would act cruelly toward us.
You do not acknowledge the Lord your Creator, and you boast of yourself as though you were the Lord your Creator.

You exalt yourself through the work of your hands and through your idols, until the Lord humiliates you, brings you down into the pit of Gehenna, and takes vengeance on you for every offense and sin you have committed on earth.

“Woe to you [?] and those like you, who do not acknowledge God, who created you, and do not know his commandment or his word! For you will repent where repentance is of no use, when you are scourged by the torment of Hades.

“You will never have any escape from it—you and your gods, those to whom you offer sacrifices and bow down as though they were God your Creator. They have neither life nor breath; they do not retaliate against anyone who harms them, nor do they do good to anyone who treats them well.

“For they are the work of human hands. Satan speaks through them to deceive the hearts of fools like you, so that he may cast you into the hell of fire—you, the idols of your gods, and the demons who obey you.
“For you do not know that there is no one who will help you. You go astray and are deceived.
“The animals God created for your food are better than you, as are wild beasts and dogs, because they have no further punishment beyond a single death.
“But you will die and then be punished again in the terror of hell, from which there is no escape forever.”
After saying this, they departed and disappeared from his sight.
But Tsirutsaydan was seized by great fear and trembling, which did not leave him until dawn.

Then he went to the place where he had thrown the bodies of the righteous, but he did not find them. He wanted to bury them, but could not find them, because God had hidden them so that he could not find any of their flesh.
He went away in pride and stubbornness of heart.

[?] For the sun stood still in the middle of the sky until he had destroyed the armies of the Canaanites, Hivites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites. He killed them too, tied their feet to their necks, and killed them with the edge of the sword; and [?] into a cave, and covered them with a stone.
He goes about in every kind of madness, evil, and disorder.
The one we spoke of earlier gnashes his teeth, roars, and devours.
Kings in a single cave. Through his prayer he stopped the sun at Gibeon so that he could destroy their armies, and he pursued at one time as many as [?].
The man who says, “My days have become like the days of heaven,” does not acknowledge God as his creator.
He thinks in his heart that the sun sets because of him.
He will rise in Gad and settle in the land of Zebulun. He will stir up war [?] Macedonia, and take provisions from Samaria, and people from Syria will give them to him.

He will settle as far as the border of Kedar and spread as far as Sidon. He will collect tribute in Achaia and raise his head as far as the Sea of Tekeze. He will turn back and spread his message as far as the Sea of Hindeke.
In this way he raises his neck as high as heaven.
He never lowers his head, but persists in every kind of evil and insolence.
All his ways lead through slippery ground, darkness, insolence, rebellion, violence, and the shedding of blood.
In all his ways he does what God hates, just as Seblanyos, his teacher, taught him: evil, violence, and [?]. He makes human beings cry out and does not care for the poor.
He also brought the kings of the nations under his power and killed them.
He judged the envoys of [?], subjugated many nations, and made them serve as he pleased.
He spared nothing, and there was nothing he did not seize, from the Sea of Tarshish to the Sea of Jericho.

He worships an idol and eats carrion, blood, torn flesh, and sacrifices offered to the gods. He has no justice; instead, all his ways are marked by injustice, wrath, anger, and turmoil. He became a terror to the nations under his hand and made them perform service as he pleased.
There is no fear of God before their eyes, for he does whatever pleases him in his presence and walks arrogantly before God his creator.
He does not regard him as his God. God will repay him according to the evil he did to his neighbor, on the day when he seizes him in his wrath.

He will take vengeance on him at that time, just as he wiped out the sinners who were before them. For he said, “I am the Lord, who takes vengeance on the proud who do not walk according to my commandments, and I will wipe their memory from the earth.”
The wicked will be repaid according to the evil they have done.
But goodness from God will follow those who do good.
And just as Joshua destroyed the kings of Canaan at one time, [?]
so it will happen to those who have provoked God by their evil deeds.
And you, O human being, are not God. Why do you exalt yourself? Today you are a human being, but tomorrow you will be earth and dust, and you will become a worm and vermin in your grave.

Moreover, hell will pursue you and those who do what you do. For your teacher is Sabellianus, who brought the sin of the whole world upon his own head because, in his pride, he led our father Adam astray.
For he refused to bow down to the work of his God, exalting himself and stiffening his neck.
You too, like your teacher, refused to [?] the Lord your God.
Kingdoms.
He took vengeance on them, and they went down into Sheol because of the evil deeds they committed on the earth.
You too will go down into Gehenna like them.
Do you think you will escape from the hand of God? For his wrath [?] worshiping God, who gave you authority over

And he tested you to see whether you would do his will or not. But if you make your way good upon the earth, God will make your paths good. Everything to which you put your hand will prosper, and he will bless you and subdue all your adversaries and enemies before you.

You rejoice in your strength, your dwelling, the fruit of your womb, your storehouses, and your pastures. Everything you point to with your fingers and think of in your heart obeys you, for God has granted you the power to act this way, to build, to plant, and to uproot.

But if you refuse to hear God's word and law and do not walk according to his judgments, you have nowhere to escape from God's hand, just like all the rebels before you who did not worship God with purity and did not trust his righteous judgment. For all his judgments are righteous.
Nothing is hidden from his eyes; everything is revealed and laid bare before him.
He is the one who seizes the authority of kings and overturns the thrones of the powerful.
He is the one who exalts the lowly and raises the fallen.
He is the one who releases prisoners, and he is the one who raises the dead. Those whose flesh has decayed and become like dust he will awaken when he wishes, for the dew of mercy comes from him.
Those who have done evil he will raise to the resurrection of judgment, because they provoked him, and he will take vengeance on them.
He will also destroy their descendants on earth, because they rebel against the law and ordinances of God.
They do not want sinners to remain in the assembly of the righteous, for the path of the righteous is more wonderful than the path of sinners.
As heaven is high above the earth, so the path of the righteous is far from the path of sinners.
But the ways of sinners are luxurious living, deceit, injustice, sexual immorality, hatred, greed, taking another person's possessions, and drunkenness in wrongdoing.

And rushing to shed blood, squandering on what is useless, making human beings weep, eating carrion and blood, eating the flesh of pigs and camels, and going in to a woman who has given birth or is menstruating, without purification.
And all this conduct of sinners is a broad road and Satan’s spread-out net, which leads to destruction and eternal condemnation.

But the way of the righteous is narrow and confined and leads to life: humility and gentleness, love and peace, fasting and prayer, purity of the body, and abstaining from foods that are not permissible—dead animals and strangled animals—and from sexual immorality and sleeping with another man’s wife.
They abstain from every filthy deed and from unclean foods that are not permitted by the law, and from filthy conduct that does not please God, for sinners do all these things.
But the righteous keep away from all the evil ways that do not please God.
And he loves them, shelters them, and saves them from all their distress.
But Satan enslaves sinners, because they observe his law, his ordinances, and everything he loves.
And you, kings and rulers, do not walk in his way. Rather, fear God, who created you and has preserved you until now.
Make the kingdom prosper.
For Balak son of Zippor, when the children of Israel came toward Amalek to take possession of the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, and the Perizzites—

He said to Balaam, “I [?] that you curse them for me, for whoever you curse is cursed, and whoever you bless is blessed. I will give you much gold and silver to honor you, so that you will curse them for me.”
And Balaam came, hoping for the reward of his wrongdoing. Balak son of Zippor showed him where the children of Israel were encamped.
He made altars, offered a sacrifice, and slaughtered sheep and cattle from among their fattened animals. He wanted to curse the children of Israel.
But God did not allow him to curse them. Instead, he turned the curse into a blessing through his words.

And he said, “May those who bless you be blessed, and may those who curse you be cursed, for you are the people whom God has chosen, and you are the dwelling place of the Beloved who comes from on high.”
Then Balak son of Zippor was grieved, enraged, and angry when Balaam blessed them in his presence, although he had commanded him to curse them.
Balaam said to him, “I will not curse those whom God has blessed, for the people whom God has chosen have come into this land.”

Balak son of Zippor said to Balaam, “I wanted you to curse them for me, but you did not curse them. Instead, you blessed them in my presence. I would have given you my house full of gold and silver if you had said, ‘Give it to me,’ and cursed them for me. But you blessed them and did not do good to me, and I will not do good to you either.”
Balaam said, “I cannot transgress or go beyond the word of God. Rather, I speak the very word that God puts into my mouth.
“I do not put wealth before my soul, for if I loved wealth, God would be angry with me, so that I would not curse a blessed people.
“For God said to Jacob their father, ‘Let those who bless you be blessed, and let those who curse you be cursed, for everyone who blesses you is blessed.’
But anyone who curses you unjustly is cursed. Make your conduct and your way good, so that God may be pleased with you.
Do not be like the people of former times, who provoked God by their wickedness. He punished them, and some he wiped out with the waters of the flood.
Others he destroyed at the hands of their enemies. He brought an enemy, a wicked people, who afflicted them and took their kings captive, together with their prophets and their Levites.
They brought them to a foreign land that they did not know, took them captive, plundered them, scourged them, and devastated their land.
And they made Jerusalem like farmland, for they tore down the towers and walls of the holy city.
The priests were taken captive, the law was cast down, and men fell in battle.
The married women were taken captive, and they did not weep for their [?] who had died, because they were taken captive and were concerned for themselves.
The children wept, and the elderly were humiliated. They showed no mercy to the old or the gray-haired.

Nor the married women, nor the virgins. They destroyed everything they found in their cities and deported them to a foreign land they did not know. For when God wishes to be angry with his people, he first brings about the destruction of his sanctuary.
For this reason, when God punished the children of Israel, God caused Jerusalem to be plowed like fields, because they continually provoke their Creator.

Yet he will by no means destroy them all together, for he has mercy on them for their fathers’ sake. It is not for their own sake that he has mercy on them, but because he loves their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who ruled in righteousness and walked [?] uprightly before their Creator.
And he established them in exalted honor, both in heaven and on earth.

Likewise, you kings and rulers who live in this passing world, remember those who came before you and walked in purity, how they inherited the kingdom of heaven and their names became honored from generation to generation.
And you too, so that he may establish your kingdom and honor your name like those good kings before you who pleased God by the goodness of their lives.
